correctness.rationale: For b with distinct primes p,q and arbitrary proposed period T, split T into support-on-b T_parallel and coprime T_perp, choose k with T_parallel|b^k and b^k>=N, and CRT u>1 with u=0 mod p, u=1 mod q and T_perp. n=b^k and m=b^k u are congruent mod T; n^n has final nonzero digit 1, while b does not divide u^m (q|b and u=1 mod q), so exactly km base-b factors are removed from m^m and F_b(m)=u^m mod b is divisible by p. This proves mixed-prime nonperiodicity for every period, not via finite search. Grau–Oller-Marcen Theorem 7 supplies all prime-power cases and Proposition 10 positive period. Independent bounded CRT witnesses confirmed 20 bases and 14 periods.
residual_risks: The prime-power classification is cited rather than reproved; its theorem is an explicit hypothesis of the complete classification.
For composite b, the final nonzero base-b digit can be nonunit; restricting to units would invalidate the argument.
